newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Reform pushes Taiwan OTC market index to new high.
newsitem.headline: Reform pushes Taiwan OTC market index to new high.

text.p: Taiwan's fledgling over-the-counter securities exchange said on Tuesday its index hit a record high on Monday after the government said it was freeing two major state funds to invest in stocks.
The OTC index on Monday ended up 5.29 points or 2.91 percent to 187.55, eclipsing the 184.22-point high recorded on May 15, an exchange official said by telephone.
Taipei announced last week it would allow the T$188 billion labour insurance fund and the T$24 billion employee pension fund to invest up to 30 percent of their values in stock.
The labour insurance fund had been barred from investing in stocks while the employee pension fund can currently invest up to 10 percent of its holdings in stocks.
The young exchange's daily turnover has risen since it introduced a new trading system in September 1995.
Up to then the daily average had been in the T$1-2 million range. Turnover on Monday was a brisk T$4.07 billion, though still below record levels seen in May.
The new system requires securities brokerages to pay only deposits to the OTC exchange before trading, rather than having to pay for shares in full at the time of purchase.
There are 69 firms listed in the OTC market, which has said it hopes to reach 100 listings by the end of 1996.
